\par\smallskip\footnotesize * optimised. $^{1}$ Azari's GBH (3 s) and CSUM (5 s) time limits are not recorded per instance. On 6$\times$10 \#20, \#21, \#23, \#29 and \#39 CSUM finds no complete solution within its 5 s and returns the GBH plan, in the campaign and in all 10 repetitions of 6 Nov 2026 (\texttt{docs/validation/data/azari\_repeat\_20261106/}), under all three time models. On 6$\times$10 \#38 under f2vert this happened in one repetition (rep04); the main objective of \#38 under f2vert spreads by 8.0 \% over the 11 runs ((max $-$ min) / min; three different plans). Of the 240 instance--time-model pairs of 5$\times$7 and 6$\times$10, 236 give the same plan in all 11 runs (campaign and 10 repetitions); on the other three (6$\times$10 f2 \#17 and \#30, f2vert \#19) the main objective spreads by at most 0.24 \%. The limits 3 s + 5 s are the paper's for the Lee \& Lee (2010) instances (Azari et al. 2017, p. 316); applying them to the Caserta instances is our choice, not the paper's. $^{2}$ Fixed-rule baselines, from their own campaign: the destination rules read no time parameter, so the plan is the same under all three time models, and its crane time is measured, not optimised.
